subject: Stabilize onramp MAP: validation window and reserve runway
messages:
From: Erin Park <erin@stratuscare.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:11:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: reserve runway + validation window for StratusCare pilot

Laura / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. We need to lock a mutual action plan that covers: a) an evaluation window (pilot traffic + perf validation), b) what capacity/reserved pool we need if we proceed to Dedicated, and c) target close date for procurement.

Constraints from our side:
- PCI-adjacent environment; procurement needs a 60-day lead window for any committed GPU spend.
- Pilot must demonstrate < 120ms p95 for chat inference at scaled concurrency (500 RPS aggregate) before procurement approval.

As a starting point, can you share a recommended GPU pool sizing (H100-equivalent), MAP milestones, and a realistic timeline to close? We want to present this to our CTO on Friday.

Attaching the initial requirements doc.

Erin Park
Head of Platform Programs
StratusCare Health

Attachment: stratus_requirements_v1.pdf
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Erin Park <erin@stratuscare.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: reserve runway + validation window for StratusCare pilot

Erin — thanks for the clear asks. Drafted a compact MAP and a capacity sketch for the scenario you described. High level answers up front:

- Recommended starting pool: 8 H100-equivalent GPUs with a short warm-up/validation phase. That gives ~500 RPS conversational headroom with batching and KV cache enabled, and allows headroom for spike protection.
- Pilot validation window: 3 weeks (1 week smoke + 2 weeks load + perf guardrails).
- Procurement lead / reservation: 60–75 days from signed MSA to delivery for dedicated capacity in the regions you mentioned; private on-prem timing will differ.

I've attached: MAP draft (xlsx) and a quick capacity CSV. Key open items for your CTO: 1) required SLO for p95 (you listed 120ms) and 2) expected concurrency distribution (percent of long vs short context).

Proposed next steps:
1) We (Redwood) run a two-week lab stress test with your sample prompts (we'll need a sanitized prompt set) — start: Mon May 18.
2) Live pilot: deploy a canary on a reserved 4-GPU pool for week 1, then ramp to 8 GPUs for weeks 2–3.
3) Procurement kickoff (if pilot passes): contract signature -> 60–75 day lead -> dedicated pool handover.

Can you confirm the pilot start window and share sanitized prompt set and a rough traffic trace? I put Rishi on the thread to confirm acceptance criteria and any procurement flex he can commit to.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: STRATUS_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx, capacity_estimate_H100_v2.csv
From: Erin Park <erin@stratuscare.com>

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: reserve runway + validation window for StratusCare pilot

Laura — this looks actionable and it hits the main concerns. A couple of clarifications from the CTO:

- The 120ms p95 target is non-negotiable for the pilot. If you can show sustained p95 < 120ms with the 8-GPU plan at expected concurrency, procurement will greenlight.
- We can provide a sanitized prompt set and a 3-day traffic trace for lab testing.
- Payment/procurement: we have limited flexibility on lead time, but can prioritize if we sign a letter-of-intent.

Request: can Rishi or Neha map the MAP milestones to procurement gating events (legal signed LOI -> finance approval -> purchase order -> delivery) with dates so we can show the timeline to internal stakeholders?

Thanks — Erin
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Erin Park <erin@stratuscare.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: reserve runway + validation window for StratusCare pilot

Erin — looping procurement gating into the MAP below (dates assume LOI signed within 5 business days after pilot start). I put conservative buffers for hardware lead times.

- Day 0 (LOI signed): finance initiates capital approval (est. 5 business days).
- Day 5–20: contract finalization + security questionnaire closure (SOC2 evidence handoff window).
- Day 21: PO issued by customer -> Redwood confirms tranche and schedules allocation.
- Day 22+60: hardware procurement and staging (60 calendar days typical for dedicated pools; up to 75 in constrained quarters).
- Day 85+: delivery, acceptance testing, and final cutover.

If StratusCare can sign a non-binding LOI earlier (we can accept an LOI before the pilot completes), we can start long-lead procurement pre-staging which often shaves ~10–14 days off the delivery date. That requires an agreed-upon baseline capacity (we recommended 8 H100-equivalent).

Action items for both teams:
- StratusCare: share sanitized prompts + 3-day trace by Fri May 15.
- Redwood (Rishi): schedule lab validation slot May 18–29 and share test plan.
- Redwood (Neha): finalize a one-page MAP timeline that explicitly maps to procurement gates for the deck to your CTO.

I can also flag this with our ops lead if you want a commitment window that shortens the lead time in exchange for a partial prepayment.

-Rishi
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Erin — following Rishi's note, attached is the one-page MAP timeline mapped against procurement gates for your CTO deck. Summary of the final MAP milestones and dates (assuming LOI signed by May 17):

- May 18: Redwood lab validation begins (sanitized prompts + trace received).
- May 25: Smoke pass complete. 
- May 26 - Jun 8: Live pilot (canary -> full pilot ramp to 8 GPUs). Performance sign-off required by Jun 8.
- Jun 9: LOI -> finance approval window starts (5–10 business days).
- Jun 20: PO issuance target (contingent on finance).
- Aug 19: Estimated dedicated pool delivery (60 days from PO).

Notes / risks:
- If StratusCare signs LOI before May 26, Redwood can begin long-lead procurement earlier and potentially deliver by Aug 5 (best case).
- Acceptance criteria: p95 < 120ms on pilot traffic for 3 consecutive days during the live pilot ramp.

I'll be your point for the MAP deck and will post the one-pager to the Drive link. If you want, we can do a 15-min CTO sync Friday to walk through the procurement gating.
